utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You know, if he can cite the page because the Court -- in my attempt to try to get through this yesterday, we didn't cover the 15th, with all due respect to my colleague, but I would be happy if he could cite for me the page where he claims I covered this part. He covered it in his cross-examination. I think I have a right on redirect, but I'll be patient with the Court, obviously, since you've been more than patient with me. If the Court wants me to move to another date or intercept, I'll kindly do so. I just want to know that if they are going to tell me that I cited it yesterday or the day before, that they should at least provide me with that page, which I can assure them I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you provide Mr. Ostojic with the reference; and you, Mr. Ostojic, is this question meant to open the way for further question on the same issue or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe not, Your Honour. But I'll move on to the 16th. They can read it, and if he can come back to me on that, I would highly appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Looking at the 16th of July, sir, and I'm sorry we're jumping around, but the 16th of July at 1111 hours. And my learned friend can interrupt me at any time if he finds it in the last two days. At 1111 hours, we talk about this involved the word "triage" and your definition and obviously the intercept that follows several hours later with this female called Jelena and this other Djurdjic. But this one at 1111 hours, you also put a positive sign there. My question to you with respect to this intercept, the only identity that you found in connection with this is that, one, the operator suggests that it's Ljubo Beara at the top, a person is asking for Beara, and then someone answers with a C designation "Ljubo." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did the Prosecution since they carry the burden of proof and want you to look at statements, did they give you the testimony of the other participants of this conversation such as this gentleman Cerovic or Turkula? Did they provide that to you to see who actually was involved in this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't see any conceivable basis for a question like this. Its legality is, I think my colleague well knows, is completely -- it is a completely inappropriate question; and, as my colleague well knows -- as my colleague well knows, we provided him with information directly related to this intercept. And I can go into private session if need be in order to explain it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I -- we don't need to do that. The question can be divided into different parts, and certainly the first part is not tenable. It is not acceptable. I mean, but the second part of the question could stand, and you could rephrase it by asking the witness what he was provided by the Prosecution, and leave it at that, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Remetic, did you hear the honourable President just now? Can you just tell us what you were provided with in connection with this conversation, whether you were provided any statements or testimony with the other participants?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any material whatsoever on this issue, no statements. I think that today I have been asked that question, and I'm already tired after three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was asked whether this was a conversation with Cerovic. Supposedly Colonel Cerovic in this purported conversation was the one who identified Mr. Beara at 1111, and based on that, I put the plus mark. As for the 15th of July, I put the signs based on the data provided by the operators. Whether they were right or not, it wasn't up to me to say. I also completely questioned the credibility and veracity of these three conversations that were put together afterwards. It is written there, the name Beara, and that is why I put the positive mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and I apologise. I know it's taking a little longer, Mr. Remetic. I just have a couple of more questions. I want to go back to my learned friend yesterday -- or today was talking about a section in your report on page 14 where you state "infallible command." And I think I understand what they're trying to suggest, but let me go and look at that section, which is in the middle of the paragraph. And again, I think I objected, and I wanted to put it in a little better context. If we could look at the sentence before that because that's what I think is relevant to keep it in context. You state as follows, and it's on page 14, and you state by saying this: "The situation today shows that Mr. Beara has definitely not forgotten the Cakavian dialect spoken in Split, and he is furthermore aware of the distinctive (distinguishing) relations between Ekavian, Ikavian, and Ijekavian, Bosnian, Montenegrin, Serbian dialects and pronunciations..." Then you go on to say that in your opinion he has an infallible command of those three. You're telling us -- tell us what you mean by that. Are you saying that he was able to switch and he either knew he was being listened to over these telephone conversations that they purport or allege against Mr. Beara? What do you mean by that, that he is aware and has these distinctive and distinguishing relations between the three dialogues?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here are two questions, basically. First, let us clarify what the command of distinctions mean. If you have a person who speaks five languages but uses only one but he does know how to say the same phrase in other languages, he is using this colloquial Split dialect, although he's aware how these words would be pronounced in his native Sarajevo. He must know that. He would know how to -- these words would be pronounced in Serbia because that is where his family lives and where he spent some time. He had some fellow officers and colleagues from that region. That means that he has the command of distinctions. I didn't hear him speak fluently Ijekavian or Ekavian, but he is aware of the differences. The second part of your question is whether he did that deliberately or whether he knew that he was being listened in. Well, I think that if he knew that he was being listened in, he wouldn't be involved in any conversations, I suppose. This is a linguistic analysis. If someone is aware that they are being taped, they will probably try to avoid any conversation. However, in these intercepts, I did take into consideration one more thing. The manner of speech of the collocutor, could it be that he adapted his speech to the person's dialect at the other end of the line? I even found things like -- and I think it was on the 1st of August where in the purported speech by Beara, the predominant dialect is Ekavian, and his collocutor speaks with some Ijekavian dialect. And also, something that could be of importance. You asked me why I did not cite the opinion of the OTP. In my working version here, you can see that I added in pencil, The OTP thinks that this is the Major Ljubo Bojanovic, the duty officer of the brigade. Obviously, I received this piece of information after I finished my job. The OTP wasn't clear on who this person was, and this is what I added afterwards and after I submitted the text on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just have a couple of more, I think maybe even one question. In trying to determine whether the dialect -- or the conversations that were captured purportedly relating to Mr. Beara and seeing whether we can attribute that to Mr. Beara, we looked at the intercepts themselves. We showed you, I think, although disclosed last month, the conversation that the Prosecution had with Mr. Beara in October of 2004, so approximately four years ago. You interviewed him, so we looked at his dialect after the events. But we also showed you the audio and the transcripts of the conversation that Mr. Beara had immediately prior to July 1995 and immediately after August of 1995. Did you see any attempts by Mr. Beara to either mask or to try to cover or hide his speech pattern or dialect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. You told us in the beginning of your session on Monday that there are basically three things that a person cannot hide, and that is I think cough, love, and your dialect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the dialect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I remembered it. I remembered it. Now, did you find any evidence at all in any of these conversations that you reviewed? Did you find any evidence of anyone trying to hide or mask their dialect? I won't ask you about the other two.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. I'm already tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's the last question, and I truly -- we all appreciate it. With respect -- did you find any evidence having looked at all the -- or the documents that you reviewed, did you find any evidence of Mr. Beara trying to hide or cover up his dialect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 18 transcripts or what I listened over the weekend or all of that together?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN REMETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could never trace any intentional attempt on his part to hide. In the transcript that I heard, one of those here, for example, two forms, like "sta se dogadja," were sufficient for me to link them to Beara as I did with the one dated the 1st of August. And if you allow me to say something at the end with relation to individual cases and words that we spent most of the time on, practice and my personal experience shows, both the one in my family and in my work, that people who are not very literate and, also, people who are highly educated intellectuals, after they have completed their military service they retain certain forms and terms and words that they continue using throughout their lives, even dating back to the era of Austria-Hungaria when they served in the Austria-Hungarian army in the German language, they retained the words such as "zuruck." Even from illiterate people, they would instead of get up, say "steh auf," which is a German form, and this is what was picked up during their military service. I know of a case of the man when the US was providing aid to Europe after the Second World War, and they sent aid per capita, and many children were born in that period. And one man was giving the name of his children, and when he came to the last or the tenth child he said "fertig," which in German means "that's finished." Later on he was asked when is Fertig starting school because he thought that "fertig" was the name. My father would always say turn to the left, which is something remnant from his army days. So these details that come from the military experience stay there forever, and I think that we wasted a lot of time on them quite unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too. Is that the end of your redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know you are about to discharge the witness, but there is an issue related to his testimony that I would like to bring to the attention of the Court, but I need to do it outside his presence as it relates to -- possibly related to the subject of further examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Professor, Professor, we've come hopefully to the end of your testimony. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I'm very grateful to you for having been very patient with the two lawyers in particular and for having accepted to come over and give testimony in this case. On behalf of everyone here present I also wish you a safe journey back home. Now, madam usher will accompany you outside the courtroom, but please stay here for the next 15 minutes or so because we might need to recall you if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your attention over the past three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. During the course of the redirect examination, the witness stated at page 48 - I think it's -- looks like it's line 6 through line 10 - in any event, he stated in reference to Mr. Ostojic's question, "the second part of your question is whether he did that deliberately or think that if he knew" -- I'm sorry -- "I think that if he knew he were -- was being listened in, he wouldn't be involved in any conversation, I suppose. This is a linguistic analysis. If someone is aware that they are being taped, they probably try to avoid any conversation." And what I provided Mr. Ostojic with yesterday was a document that we received yesterday. It is 3628 on my exhibit list, which I avoided using with this witness, but it is a document authored by Mr. Beara that relates to the capacity of the -- I've given you the wrong 65 ter inadvertently, but it's dated 1st September, 1995. It's a document that is authored by Mr. Beara, and it relates to the capacity of the opposing forces to intercept their VRS communications. In addition to that, it references an intercept as an example of people speaking openly on the lines in the face of that knowledge. It is a document that is likely to come in through -- at some point against Mr. Beara, but in light of what the witness has said about Mr. Beara's knowledge concerning being listened in on, I thought it would be appropriate to put it to this witness as to whether or not this effects his testimony or his conclusions as concerns his review of those intercepts. Clearly, it's a discretionary issue for you since he has effectively concluded his testimony, but I thought it would be appropriate and fair to put it to him at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I never received a document dated the 1st of September, 1995. Yesterday I was given a document from the 13th of August, 1995, so I'm not sure if we're on the same page here. I have the document that he provided to me yesterday. I certainly would like to know where they receive the information and a little more background, and then I can possibly formulate a position in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, there is disagreement, obviously, on whether this document has been provided to Mr. Ostojic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then I'm also told, and I don't -- this is -- I'm told this, that where Mr. Vanderpuye points to the transcript that the witness said this is linguistic analysis, I'm being told that he actually said the opposite. We can check that. I don't remember it personally, but it that he said the opposite, that it is not linguistic analysis, but I didn't catch that at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I remember, that he said -- that's what I remember, that he said it isn't a linguistic analysis. In effect --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will withdraw it. There's some issues with respect to -- there are some issues with respect to the disclosure of the document to Mr. Ostojic in all fairness to him, and so I would propose we deal with it another time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. In the meantime, then we can discharge the witness for good.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Documents, exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that we have tendered our list to the Court, and there's nothing to add other than what's reflected on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, any objections? There are three four, five, nine documents that are being tendered as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There are no objections to my colleague's exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objections from the other Defence teams? I wouldn't imagine so. There being no objections, these documents are being admitted. You also have some documents you wish to tender, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I see a list of three, six, eight, nine documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, you don't need to go through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I believe that you have it already, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it has been circulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic in particular, do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So also, these nine documents are being admitted, and we can now call, at last, the next witness Mrs. Svetlana Gavrilovic. For the record, I notice that in the meantime during this session, Mr. Mitchell has joined the Prosecution team in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's just past noon, madam, so it's good afternoon, and you are very much welcome to this Tribunal. Mr. Ostojic, who is lead counsel defending Mr. Beara, has summoned you as a witness in Defence. Before you start giving your testimony, you are requested under our rules to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. Madam usher has just given you the text. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn declaration with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Please make yourself comfortable. I think everyone will be making an effort to finish -- go through your testimony today so that you don't have to stay here any longer. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, although it wasn't our fault, I do apologise to you for having kept you waiting yesterday, but the testimony of the previous witness went beyond what was expected. I hope you understand and you will bear with us. Mr. Ostojic will go first with some questions. I think he will then be followed by one or more other lawyers, particularly from the Prosecution side, if at all, and then you can go home. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Nikolic will lead this witness with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't know that. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Nikolic, please introduce yourself in case you haven't met the witness already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We have already met, but this is the official part of your testimony. I'm going to introduce myself and give you some guidelines for today. I'm Predrag Nikolic. I represent Mr. Ljubisa Beara, and I will examine today on behalf of the Defence team. Before I ask you to introduce yourself, I would like to tell you that we are both being interpreted, and we would like to give the interpreters time to interpret us correctly, which means that you should wait before providing your answer to allow the interpreters to do their job properly. Could you please introduce yourself for the record.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Svetlana Gavrilovic. I was born in Belgrade, and I reside in Belgrade. What else am I supposed to say to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slowly. It is customary for every witness to tell us about their educational background.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I completed primary school, grammar school, and then I completed my university education at the department of defectology, oligophrenological department for mentally handicapped children, and later it just so happened that I directed my profession towards beauty treatments, cosmetics.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your profession, did you ever engage in your profession at all?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a year, and after that one year my husband signed a contract with a Yugoslav company that had operations in Baghdad in Iraq. He went there, and since it was difficult for me to engage my profession proper because I did not speak the language, I decided to take up another profession that would be marketable anywhere in the world. That's how I became a beautician, and I continued doing that if even if -- after I returned from Iraq.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Gavrilovic, when were you in Iraq?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: We were in Iraq from the end of 1975 to 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Upon your return from Iraq, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: We resided in Belgrade, and I continued working as a beautician because I liked the job and I didn't want to change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You know Ljubisa Beara and his family?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know them. I've known them since 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Under what circumstances and how did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: My girlfriend from Belgrade socialized with the Beara family, and since their younger son had problems with adolescent complexion she called me one day and asked me if I could treat the son of her friends, and that's how I first met the younger son who came to see me for his problems, and then I met his father, mother, ie., Mr. Beara and his wife Nada.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How often did you visit each other, or rather, a chance encounter, did it later on grow into a friendship?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It became a true friendship because my husband had a lot in common with Mr. Beara. My husband was a keen model maker, and Mr. Ljubisa Beara is also a model maker. He -- Mr. Beara made models of sail ships, and they had a lot in common and they had a lot to talk about. Both Mr. Beara and his wife are well educated people, and sometimes when we would visit them and especially the first time we visited them, I saw a library full of books. And since I am a keen reader, I asked them if I could borrow one of their books to read and he said, yes, of course. I chose a few books that I was interested in, and then he took a book from a shelf with little cards, and then he said, okay, I have a list of all of my books, I will make a note of your name and date so that you know that you will return the books. I found this very surprising, but he explained that he always does that with anybody who borrows his books. In other words, we always had lot to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So he was a good person for socialising. Can you tell me where Mr. Ljubisa Beara's family reside?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: They reside in Kosovska Street in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned their younger son?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His name is Branco, who was my client.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And what was Mrs. Beara's name?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Nada.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In addition to the issues that you had in common and topics that you had in common, did you have any others that brought you closer together?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the children were very interesting children. The older son, who is a teacher of English, and his wife, who is teacher of Serbian in grammar school, we always joked around; our conversations were always pleasant, and Nada is a good cook, and she always served good food, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You said just a moment ago that you met them towards the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts. The end of 1992 or the beginning of 1992. I wouldn't be able to tell you correctly, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So if I'm not mistaken, this is when you started socialising?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You know that at that time the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina was already on?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. I think leading. On this topic, I think, and these date issues, any sort of leading questions about dates and times and places is absolutely off limits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is understandable because at the end of the day the bottom line in relation to the witness, the testimony of this witness is what happened on a particular day. So no direct questions, please. No leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I thought that it was a generally -- or notorious fact what happened in Yugoslavia and that we were all aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to these kind of things. What is and what is not, this is -- I don't think counsel is doing it on purpose, but I think we should ask -- encourage him not to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also don't think counsel is doing it on purpose, but I think he now understands. He has got to follow a certain practice, a certain line, and we'll try to stick to that. If you want to discuss further with Mr. Ostojic, we'll give you a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Madam, during that period of time or after your initial encounter with the Beara family, how often did you see them?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly, but I would say that it was always on the occasion of some celebration, an anniversary, children's birthday parties, our own birthday parties, religious holidays, mostly things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You mentioned birthday parties. Does this mean -- or rather, did you know the birthdays of Ljubisa Beara and others?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was born on the 14th of July because I was also born in July, and we would very often joke about that, and we would say that we were all -- both born under the same sign of Capricorn [as interpreted] who looks strong from the outside, and that's how I know when he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I apologise. What is the horoscope sign of you and Ljubisa Beara?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Cancer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This was just for the transcript, to clarify a mistake in the transcript. Did you meet every year on his birthday or not?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It depended on when he was there, whether we were invited. Whenever he was and we were invited, then we would go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When was it the last time that you met for his birthday?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It was the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How do you remember that it was in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I remember because it was a so-called silver wedding anniversary of my husband and me. That's the 25th anniversary, which is a significant anniversary in our country, the 25th anniversary of wedding. This is something that you remember. We got married in 1970 on the 4th of January, and we wanted to mark the 25th anniversary of our marriage by taking a trip on the Orient Express. When the weather got better in the spring or in the summer, when we inquired about the price of that journey, unfortunately we had to give up on that idea because we had realised that we wouldn't be able to finance that. And on the 14th of July when the Bearas -- when -- Mira and Toma actually invited us because Ljubisa Beara had come to their place. They invited us, their place, and on that particular evening we spoke about our 25th wedding anniversary and the journey that we were supposed to take on the Orient Express that did not come through.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you please slow down a little, and since we are talking about this birthday party, you mentioned the names of the persons who invited you. Could you please repeat those.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: They were Toma Bozinovic and Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Where did you meet?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: We met at Toma and Mira's house in Belgrade in Sumatovacka Street. There's where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, who was there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously the host, Toma and Mira were there; my husband and I; Ljubisa Beara and his wife Nada; and only briefly Dr. Djordje, who was Toma's mother's personal physician. He dropped by to bring some medicines. He only stayed for one drink. He was in a haste on a house call to another visit. That's why he had to leave so early.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive at the house on that day, at Mira and Toma's house?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the evening. I had worked, and my husband, when they invited us, went there around 8 o'clock, and I had some things to finish because I had a complicated procedure and I could not leave earlier; therefore, I left the office around 9, and that's when I went to their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please remember, given the details that you mentioned around your anniversary, was your anniversary a topic of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about the Orient Express, I about our wish to take a journey on that train for our 25th anniversary, but we did not have enough money. Yes, we spoke about that. Toma joked and said there was a nearly opened newly opened restaurant in new Belgrade that looks like a carriage of the Orient Express train, so you can go there and just imagine that you are sitting on the actual train. I remember that remark of his very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Gavrilovic, did you know that Ljubisa had come from the frontline?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that, but I did not know in what capacity. I never asked him them that. I was not interested in that. I never wished to know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's already there but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a classical, typical direct question, leading question, that you should avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we also have one brief moment outside the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Gavrilovic, do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit, not well. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I think she needs to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not sufficiently well enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a break now. You can leave the courtroom. We'll reconvene in 25 minutes' time. Madam usher, if you could accompany the witness first, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to give you an indication of what I have on this witness in terms of a summary, that this witness knows Beara family through mutual friends. Her late husband Djordje was from a diplomatic family and had part of his schooling in France. Therefore, he used to jokingly link Beara's birthday on July 14th to the French national holiday, the Bastille Day. Witness and her husband received a call from a friend, Mira Cekic - I'm now hearing Mira Bojanovic - inviting them to come over on the evening of the 14th because Beara was in town from the Republika Srpska to celebrate his birthday. She recalls that occasion because there was a 25th anniversary -- was her 25th anniversary, and an Orient Express trip had been planned with her husband, had fallen through, which was the subject of the conversation at the party. That's it. There's lots of other information here relating to different -- very important facts related to an alibi. I don't have it. I would ask that this witness be delayed and that I be given a summary of what they intend to have this witness testify to and so that I can at least have that summary. I hate it to come to this point, but I don't how else to do it. The -- we see that she says, for example, that she is able to connect this birthday with the fact that they share the same birthday and the same sign. I don't see that here. I don't have that. In fact, it's something else in this. So if -- clearly, they've got an outline. They know what she's going to say. If they could help us with that so we have that so we can be better prepared so we don't have to delay cross-examination, and that's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nikolic or Mr. Ostojic, I don't know who wishes to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll address the Court if I can on this and maybe help my learned friend. During the break we spent -- or at least all of us did but I did in particular with the Prosecution trying to resolve any issues they may have. With other witnesses, they asked for more information. They wrote to us; we met with them; we wrote back; we provided detailed information to them as we knew it. Some of the information we didn't have, so we were in the field, as I was during that period. For this particular witness, they never asked or queried as to whether or not they had adequate or sufficient information. We assumed as we do with other witnesses when we give them a summary that they can call us if they think it's inadequate. They didn't call us. They didn't mention this witness at all, so we didn't provide them anything other than that which we had at the time, and I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you are answering the question or the issue raised by Mr. McCloskey. Mr. McCloskey is referring to bits and pieces of evidence, facts that are resulting now during her evidence as a result of direct questions that are being put to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The only comment I can make with respect to that is, I don't know when her birthday is. I know that it's not -- I know when Mr. Beara's birthday is as I do mine. We can provide that information. We gave him dates and names and birth dates, places of birth for all of the witnesses that they inquired. I didn't know about this woman Mira Cekic, who is a witness. I didn't know about this Mira Bojanovic. I'll find out. That might be her late husband's name. She -- I'll find out if it's a different name. I think it's the same person. I can find it out. I honestly don't know that as I sit here who Mira Bojanovic is or however she spoke it, but I will inquire it, and I'll find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I won't go over all the times we've been asking. You probably remember our first time when we asked for alibi evidence and there was a court order for that. It doesn't get much more than alibi evidence than this stuff that we are hearing. I also have an e-mail from Ms. Dzambazovic dated 25 August basically saying they had a proofing session with this witness and others, and there's no further information obtained. So if we could get a reasonable outline of what is to come. They know it's coming. I know they know it's coming. They're -- we can see how well prepared Mr. Ostojic was for his last witness. I think they are well prepared for this witness, and if we could get some of that information --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. Mr. President, I can -- we'll provide him -- at the break, he can sit down with us, tell us what he wants. We'll provide it to him. I don't think it's that big of a deal. I do want to address the issue that Mr. McCloskey keeps raising, and that's alibi. We take a different view of that. He had an opportunity to raise that issue either by way of a motion or before the Court. He's throwing this out there, and I do take exception to it. The whereabouts of Mr. Beara are relevant. I don't consider this to be alibi as I think Mr. McCloskey feels that it is, and I think we can address that with the Court and perhaps we should because I know other accused who are in custody, recently who were brought to custody recently weren't at certain sites but everyone knows where they were. It's not an alibi that someone was in Pale, but we have different view given that the indictment talks about the third variant Joint Criminal Enterprise. I don't know why he keeps mentioning it. It's not a surprise that their evidence with respect to Mr. Beara is grossly thin, in my opinion. I don't think they can establish his whereabouts even from their witnesses. We tried very hard to establish areas where there is no such evidence, areas where there's suspect evidence. We're bringing forth experts like Professor Remetic and Professor Wagenaar, witnesses that they've known about for months and weeks. But I do want to address this issue of alibi, not necessarily now, but I want to address it when they're prepared, and I don't think that they are, with all due respect, to discuss it fully with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the Court understands our position on alibi. We haven't pushed that since the orders and the lack of substance regarding legal alibi. I use it in that to remind the Court and counsel that we've asked for information related to the whereabouts of Mr. Beara on key times, and all we've got is this, and now we've got material contradictory to that, key material related to this issue of where he is, and counsel's resisting. We have -- we're frankly -- this is the first of other alibi witnesses. I've already explained to you as you recall the witness that provided the alibi on direct testimony of him being somewhere on the 11th of July for the first time. This is a continuing of that. All I ask for is what -- a better outline of this, and I would ask that this witness be removed for the time being until we can get something on this topic. They've got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we've heard enough. I think we've heard enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are clear now in our mind on this and unanimous. First, I think you should utilize the next 25 minutes to meet, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Nikolic, to cross the Ts and put the dots on the Is and try to indicate exactly what the rest of the evidence is going to be about. We will continue with the evidence, then depending on whether there is an agreement between you or not or whether -- and what the outcome of the rest of the testimony will be, if you have problems with proceeding with your cross-examination, we will consider your submissions and react accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break now of 25 minutes. That means we'll reconvene at -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will withdraw my request. I have had so many of these meetings that I don't find there's any reasonable chance of it being productive. I can't get an interpreter at -- this late, in the middle of lunch. This will totally disrupt my ability to conduct further cross. I apologise. I know you are trying to get this accomplished, but I will withdraw my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a break. We'll reconvene at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nikolic, please try to restrict yourself to questions that go to the substance of what is contained in your summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Gavrilovic, you mentioned in your previous answer Mira and Toma Bozinovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please, how long do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Mira's father and my mother were born in the same place, so I've known Mira from the time when we were teenagers. When she married Toma, I also met him, so that means quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I conclude from your answer that these are spouses?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was Mira's maiden name?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Her maiden name was Cekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What is Mira by profession?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: She finished the PTT secondary school, and she was employed with Telecom Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What about her husband? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He was involved in distribution of flowers in Belgrade and other towns around Serbia. I know that Nada, Ljubisa's wife, because she is a horticulturist, an engineer or horticulturer, was working for a Split-based flower distributor, and I know that they cooperated within the business environment, and that is how they met each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let us go back now to the party that you mentioned. Can you just repeat who was there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: The hosts, Toma and Mira; Nada and Ljubisa; my husband and I; and I mentioned the doctor who just dropped by. His name was Djordje. He was a cardiologist, and he dropped by just to leave some medicines for Toma's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What was the profession of your husband?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He finished secondary school in Paris, France, because his father was at the time the representative of the Yugoslav Tourist Association. He finished the post-secondary school of economics in Belgrade and was employed with a representative office of the US-based company called Caterpillar, and as such he was sent to work in Iraq.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm sorry to ask you, is your husband alive?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No. He died in 2001 of lung cancer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: What about Toma Bozinovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He is also dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know when he died?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Toma Bozinovic died about a year after my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Madam, can you recall the topic of the conversation among the individuals that you mentioned at the party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you, what I remember is -- was this unfortunate Orient Express that we did not manage to travel on and the jokes that we made about that. Then yes, Ljubisa, it was his birthday that evening. He was smartly dressed. That's what I noticed. He had a light blue shirt and a dark blue summer blazer with golden buttons, double breast, rows of buttons. And I did tell him, oh, God, how handsome you look, and then I said to Nada, Nada, how did you manage to keep such a handsome man for yourself for so many years, and we also joked about this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at this birthday party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately until midnight or just after midnight, so let's say about three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you continue to see the Beara family later on?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did, on various occasions, or if we were walking and passing by their house we would ring the bell and have a coffee with them if they were in, either Nada alone or both of them or when their children were with them because their son and their daughter-in-law do not live in Belgrade. When they came to visit, we would also go and see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After your husband's death, did you continue to see them?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Since my husband was very good with his hands, I never had to call any handymen to do any repairs in my home, and when after he was gone, and I knew that Ljubisa was also a good handyman capable of doing various things, I would call Nada and ask if Ljubisa was available to come over to fix my iron or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm sorry I have to go back to these sad events relating to your husband. I would like to ask you whether all your friends attended the funeral of your husband?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 5th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Beara there as well?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is where Mr. McCloskey is definitely right. You obviously had prior insight into this information because otherwise you wouldn't have asked the question. But this is not included in the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order to resolve this, with this I'm going to conclude the questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then conclude, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Gavrilovic. I've finished with my questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean I'm free to leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, not yet. Mr. Zivanovic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krkvic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My name is Peter McCloskey. I'm working for the Office of the Prosecutor. Can you tell me when you first started thinking back about this alleged birthday party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic contacted me in Belgrade. He introduced himself as a lawyer on the Beara Defence team, and he asked me whether I would be willing if I remembered the date, the 14th of July, whether I would be able to talk to him, whether I would be willing to testify about that, and since that moment I've been thinking about that. This was maybe two months ago or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So about two months ago Mr. Stanic came up to you and asked you specifically about the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me whether I remembered the 14th of July, 1995, where I was, and what I did on that date, and that is when I remembered precisely because of our wedding anniversary, Ljubisa's birthday, the whole story. I did remember that on that evening I attended Ljubisa's birthday party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you told him that then and there in response to his question about 14 July?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So after about 13 years' time, a person asks you a specific date and you are able without talking to anyone, referring to anything, remember a birthday party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because of my silver wedding anniversary and the Orient Express, because we joked about it and we discussed our failure to go on this trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understand anyone would remember their 25th wedding anniversary year and date, of course, and might, of course, remember any big plans they had to take that date or year, certainly. But I don't see how you having those memories can go back 13 years and remember off the top of your head a conversation at a birthday party about the Orient Express; but you did that, no problem, huh?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I said to Ljubisa maybe too rashly without thinking how handsome he looked, and then I apologized to Nada for saying that, and that is how I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was his hair like, Mr. Beara's?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He had grey hair. Greyish hair, but he had more grey hairs than dark hairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, was it white or grey?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps greyish white.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long was it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Short. Normal short hair. I mean, it wasn't long. He wasn't bald, but he had short hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you see anybody here who -- can you just tell us roughly, and I don't know want you to worry about Mr. Beara. We know time goes on for all of us, but anybody here whose hair looks roughly the same length at Mr. Beara's was at the time?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: This gentleman over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The fellow that's smiling, Mr. Krkvic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. And after 13 years you remember his shirt?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am a very perceptive person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know his birthday was on the specific date of 14 July? I'm told Cancer is between June 22nd and July 22nd, but you remembered that right off. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you told that was his birthday before you said it, or did you say it first?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I said it because the 14th of July is the date of the fall of Bastille. My husband finished his secondary school in France, and he always used to tell us how in France this date is celebrated, and every 14th of July I would tease him by saying, oh, this is one of your youth holidays and celebrations. Probably, that's what prompted my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I don't know about Serbia, but certainly Bastille Day is remembered. But the 14th of July, how is it you connect the 14th of July to Mr. Beara, 13 years after the fact or before?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I made a connection earlier because as I said, every 14th of July ever since I married my husband I used to tease him on that day by saying that that was his holiday, so we joked about this, and the coincidence was that it was Ljubisa's birthday on the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what other birthday parties had you been to about -- to Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That was the last one. I may have been on one occasion before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us about that one before that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was in their house. Their children came too. We were sitting and talking. We talked about various things, mostly about the books we read because my husband and Mr. Beara were involved in a discussion about their hobbies, about the material, where they could purchase it, et cetera, so basically this is what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what year was that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we met in 1992, in late 1992, early 1993, so that was the first year of our acquaintanceship.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you are not sure about that birthday. What date was that party for that other birthday, the one previous?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Probably the 14th when his birthday was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you don't know the date?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: The 14th. The 14th of July. That's his birthday, on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, you said probably the 14th of July. Now you are sure it was the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying is that his birthday is on the 14th of July. Whether it was in -- whether in 1993 it was celebrated precisely on the 14th of July, I cannot remember exactly, but that was the reason for us to get together and celebrate his birthday with a couple of drinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's the same for 1995, isn't it? You remember getting together for a birthday, but you don't remember what date in particular?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I remember exactly that in 1995 it was the 14th of July, and the reason for me to remember that is my wedding anniversary, and what my husband and I wanted to give to each other as a present, that is, a trip on the Orient Express, and that is why I remember that it was on the 14th of July in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was the date of your wedding anniversary?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Our wedding anniversary was on the 4th of January, but on the 14th of July we discussed our 25th anniversary. That evening, we talked about the Orient Express and the 25th wedding anniversary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The fact that you had a wedding anniversary on the -- January somehow makes you connect with precisely the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because when I noticed that Ljubisa was looking handsome and well dressed, we started making jokes about that. Then we started talking about marriages, about their wedding, about Ljubisa's and Nada wedding. Then we moved to our wedding, and that is brought to the subject of our 25th anniversary and how we had wanted to go, of course, not in January. We wanted to go when the weather got better, and that is how this conversation started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what conversations did you have on the previous birthday, the one that you think might be 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you are sure?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember any specific topic. I cannot remember exactly. We talked about general topics that we always discussed. We made jokes, told jokes, how life was passing, how we were getting older, and just the usual stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was Mr. Beara wearing during that first birthday?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Since it was in their house, he was casually dressed in a T-shirt. It was warm. We were sitting on the balcony, and he had a T-shirt and a pair of jeans or some casual trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sleeveless T-shirt or one with sleeves?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: The one with sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: White one with some logo on it. I don't remember what it read, but there was something written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was it one of those V-necks or --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It was close to his neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about his shoes?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Slippers. Slippers. Summer slippers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What kind of slippers? What colour?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about on his birthday on the 14th of July, 1995? What kind of shoes was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He had dark shoes, black shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When was the first time that Ljubisa Beara came over to your house to fix something after your husband died?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date, but this may have been maybe three or four months later. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did he do?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He fixed my iron.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was he wearing then?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a navy coat that he took off, and then he remained wearing a shirt, a sweater on top of the shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the 1995 birthday, what day of the week was that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know what day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you work on Sunday? Did you work on Sunday in July?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Since my salon is in my house, in my apartment, I will work. If I have cases that require daily therapy, then I will work even on Sundays.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you work on the Sunday before or after the -- well, the birthday? Before, after, or on the birthday?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: On the day of the birthday I did work, but I can't remember whether it was Sunday or what other day, and I did work both the Sunday before and the Sunday after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Saturday?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, again, yes, if the therapy so requires. If you have to see a person for ten consecutive days, and there are such treatments, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think -- I'm told that the 14th of July, 1995, was on a Friday, but you didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, no. I didn't know that it was Friday. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you told us that you had a big job that day at your beauty shop. How about that Saturday? Did you work in your beauty shop the Saturday after the party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Again, that was a treatment that finished on the Saturday. That was a treatment that went from the previous Saturday to the Saturday next week. It's a treatment with antibiotics and some other agents that have to be applied every day if you want them to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where had Mr. Beara been prior to you seeing him at this party?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where he was. I know that on that day when Mira and Toma had invited us that he was at their place. They told us he would be there, and he indeed was, and I don't know about the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, what did Mr. Stanic tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic just asked me if I could remember the 14th of July, 1995, what I did on that day, and then I told him what I did. I told him that in the evening of that day Mira and Toma had invited us to come to their place because Nada and Ljubisa were there. It was Ljubisa's birthday, and they invited us to celebrate Ljubisa birthday together with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How long did you spend with Mr. Stanic a couple of months ago?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour, 40 minutes, not more than that. He contacted me first, asked me whether he could come to my place to talk to me. He came. This is what he asked me. I told him what I knew, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When was the next time you spoke to anybody from the Beara team?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: It was again Mr. Stanic who called me and asked me if I would be willing to repeat my story publicly in court, everything that I had previously told him, and I said that I would, why not, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When was that that he contacted you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the second time around when he asked me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: That was a month ago, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And after speaking to him the first time a couple of months ago, can you give us a date when you actually first spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't. I can't give you the date. I can't remember. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know the month?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it may have been in April, in the month of April, March or April when I met with Mr. Stanic, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What day?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't. I did not consider this date worth retaining, remembering at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I know in answering that question you kind of looked at me and smiled as if, how am I going -- supposed to remember that date, right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, right. I really don't remember that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Stanic tell you what your testimony was going to be about? I mean, what Mr. Beara's case was about?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No. He asked me specifically whether I remembered what I had done on the 14th of July, on that day, that evening in 1995, and I told him what I have just repeated to you here, and he never told me anything about Mr. Beara or anything to that effect. Mr. Stanic never mentioned anything to that effect. He only asked me if I remembered anything that happened on the 14th of July, and if I did, what it was. And he also told me that he was on Beara's defence team. That's how he introduced himself, and then he asked me about the 14th of July. I told him what I did, and he said, very well, then, and then he asked me whether I would be willing to repeat that if necessary, and I said that I would. There you go. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you think he meant when he said the Beara Defence team? Defence for what, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know anything at all, but I assumed that that date must be important for Ljubisa Beara's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Defence of what?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I knew that Ljubisa Beara was here in The Hague. I knew that, so I assumed that it was to defend him against some charges, and I really don't know what charges have been brought against him. I don't know this to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mass murder, genocide? Doesn't ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that. I know that from the media, but I don't know that Beara participated in that. I really don't know because we never discussed that. Whenever we got together before the event, after the event, during that time, we never talked about that, or at least this was not something that came up in the presence of us women. We never spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this July 14th, 1995, alleged party, this subject of Srebrenica never showed up despite it being blasted all over the airwaves, all over Belgrade, and everywhere else?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No. If any of the men wanted to raise the issue, Beara would always be the one to say, please, let's not discuss that; we are here to party, to celebrate my birthday; don't ask me about that. So we never discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, who brought it up?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: My husband was prone to asking questions of this sort, but Ljubisa Beara never wanted to discuss that or at least not when I was present. I don't know what men discussed in private, but in front of us women they never brought up the issue because Ljubisa would not allow anybody to bring up the matter in front of us women.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what was brought up about it by anybody, women to women, man to women, without Beara, about Srebrenica that night?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing on that particular day or on that particular evening. It never came up. The issue of war never came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What about having to go back to the war? Sometimes that gets mentioned during these times.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: You are asking me about that particular evening, the 14th of July, or in general terms?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 14th July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Nothing was said about that on that particular evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So a couple of months ago, maybe March or April, Mr. Stanic comes up to you and asks you about these -- this important topic; you know that Mr. Beara is in The Hague; you know about genocide and mass murder, but you cannot tell me the date of this -- that he contacted you, Stanic? You can't even tell me the month?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA GAVRILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't. I really can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm almost through, but if I could review my materials and see if I have any other questions. I notice it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No, no, I was going to invite you to finish, but having heard that I will give you the opportunity, obviously. Madam, we haven't finished. You will need to return again tomorrow. It will be for a short time, and then you will be free to go. So madam usher can escort you out of the courtroom. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
